newsitem.title: ITALY: Denim does for old, young alike at Milan shows.
newsitem.headline: Denim does for old, young alike at Milan shows.

text.p: Denim-clad grannies, muscle-bound beach bums and men in drag proved that jeans are universal at the Milan ready-to-wear women's fashion shows on Monday.

Fashion house Swish Jeans, in an uptempo show backed by toe-tapping sounds from the 1960s and 1970s, gave a lively display of mustard yellows, oranges, browns and blues in a collection which recalled styles and hemlines of the 1970s.

"We find a rainbow to escape from the metropolitan dullness," Swish Jeans said, setting the colours in rainbow stripes alongside each other on dresses and tops to illustrate its spring/summer collection for 1997.

Elderly women, half the height of supermodels Naomi Campbell and Eva Herzigova who shared the catwalk, sauntered onto the runway swinging jeans jackets, while a man strapped into a tight red leather trousersuit pouted from under an outsize black wig.

Jeans were mostly narrow legged hipsters, prints were in bold lines and drew inspiration "from the papers that were used in the 1970s to cover drawers", while skirts flared from the hip and dresses swept the floor or cut off mid-thigh.
Sinuous, silky and slashed to the hip was Italian designer RoccoBarocco's vision of what women at the cutting edge of fashion will be wearing in spring and summer 1997.

RoccoBarocco, showing his designs on the second day of the shows, paraded ankle-length sheath gowns in scarlet, black or sequinned silver, pinned at one side by a couple of diamante buckles and revealing a length of flesh from top to bottom.
Necklines were broad V-shapes, scooped wide and low or cut square while dress backs were crisscrossed or ribbed and set off by high-heeled snakeskin shoes.

The collection, opened by supermodel Naomi Campbell in a white and blue-trimmed bikini, began with a series of crisp white bathing suits cut to sit just at the top of the thigh and edged in black or navy blue.

The daytime theme continued in classic navy and white striped or chequered waisted blazers accompanied by high, wedge-heeled sandals, wide-legged white trousers with turn-ups and off-one-shoulder blue and white striped knits.

For the less conservative there were lines of transparent, short cropped blouses, tied at the waist with a high turned-up collar, as well as long figure-hugging dresses with wide white horizontal strips alternated with narrow transparent panels or see-through lace patches.
The Milan shows continue until Sunday, with the first of the big names, Miuccia Prada, kicking off early on Tuesday, followed by Gianni Versace's second line Istante in the evening.
Wednesday sees design duo Dolce & Gabbana and stylist Krizia, while Thursday and Friday bring fashion house Gucci and designer Gianfranco Ferre.
Versace presents his main collection on Saturday and Giorgio Armani closes the shows with his main collection on Sunday.
